prompt:
Add a `heading_offset` option to `markdown.Markdown` (and `markdown.markdown`): a whole number from 0 to 5, default 0, that shifts the level of every heading Markdown produces by that many (an `h1` becomes an `h2` with 1), never beyond `h6`. Any other value raises `ValueError`.
- It applies to hash and underline headings, and to headings from extensions such as `md_in_html`.
- The `toc` extension sees the shifted levels (its tokens and `toc_depth`).
- The command line gets `--heading-offset N`.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added the `heading_offset` option (0–5, default 0; any other value, including bools and floats, raises `ValueError`) and the `--heading-offset N` command-line option. Hash, underline and md_in_html headings are shifted and capped at h6, and the toc tokens and `toc_depth` use the shifted levels. The full test suite passes (112 skipped). I could not run flake8 because it isn't installed. The shift is done by a new built-in step (treeprocessor) that runs just before toc's. Plain raw HTML headings are left as written; md_in_html headings with `markdown="1"` are shifted. On the command line an out-of-range or non-integer value prints a usage error instead of a traceback. The new tests are in a new file, test_heading_offset.py, and in the existing toc, md_in_html and API test files. Docs and an [unreleased] changelog entry are added.
